findings.claim: Examine how physical and human factors have together shaped UK landscapes. (8 marks plus 4 SPaG)
findings.truth: 'Examine' is not one of this board's 12 command words. The list is Identify/State/Name, Define, Calculate, Draw/plot, Label, Describe, Compare, Explain, Suggest, Assess, Evaluate, Select...and justify. Reworded as an Assess question.
findings.evidence: spec Appendix 3 command word table; spec p.2 'consistent use of 12 different command words'

findings.claim: Examine how marine, sub-aerial and human processes interact to shape coastal landscapes in the UK. / exam tip: For 8-mark 'Examine' questions
findings.truth: Same wrong command word in the practice question and the exam tip. Reworded to Assess.
findings.evidence: spec Appendix 3 command word table

findings.claim: the underlying gault clay has been hollowed out into the Weald
findings.truth: The Gault Clay forms a narrow vale below the chalk escarpment; the Weald itself is cut mainly into the Wealden Group clays and sands. The sentence conflates the two. Not mark-affecting, so left alone.
findings.evidence: British Geological Survey mapping of the Weald anticline

findings.claim: The UK has 15 national parks (10 in England, 3 in Wales, 2 in Scotland), covering around 10% of the land.
findings.truth: The park count is right. Their combined area is about 20,000 km2, roughly 8% of the UK, so 'around 10%' is a little high but within tolerance for a rounded claim.
findings.evidence: recomputation from published park areas

findings.claim: The UK has roughly 31,000 km of coastline.
findings.truth: Coastline length is scale-dependent: about 17,800 km for the Great Britain mainland and about 31,400 km for the UK including islands at OS measurement scales. The figure is defensible as stated.
findings.evidence: Ordnance Survey coastline measurements

findings.claim: Every 8-mark question in the unit is labelled '(8 marks plus 4 SPaG)'.
findings.truth: The paper carries up to 4 SPaG marks in total, not 4 per extended-writing question. Read across ten lessons the label implies every 8-marker adds 4 SPaG. Options: (a) leave, since each lesson is read alone and one 8-marker on the paper does carry the SPaG marks; (b) change the label unit-wide to '(8 marks)' and say once that one extended-writing question on the paper also carries up to 4 SPaG marks. Recommend (b) as a corpus-wide change, not a single-unit edit.
findings.evidence: spec: 'Of the 94 marks available up to 4 marks are awarded for spelling, punctuation, grammar and use of specialist terminology'
findings.ruling: Leave (matches printed scheme / corpus-wide relabel queue).

findings.claim: Every lesson's calculation question is typed '4 marks - Calculate', e.g. '18,000,000 x 2.5' for 4 marks.
findings.truth: Calculations on this paper are short, typically 1-3 marks; awarding 4 marks for a single multiplication over-rewards. Not impossible marks, so not edited. Recommend re-tiering the ten calculation questions to 2-3 marks with matching mark schemes as one pass.
findings.evidence: spec assessment information: multiple-choice, short open, open response, calculations and 8-mark extended writing
findings.ruling: Leave (matches printed scheme / corpus-wide relabel queue).

findings.claim: Around 5 million people in England live in places at risk of flooding from the sea or rivers
findings.truth: The Environment Agency figure counts properties, not people: about 5.2 million properties in England, one in six. Lesson 5 states it correctly as homes, so the unit contradicts itself. Changed to homes and businesses.
findings.evidence: Environment Agency national flood risk assessment; L5 key fact in this unit

findings.claim: over a third of new housing in southern England in the past decade has been within 10 km of a coast or estuary
findings.truth: No such published statistic could be found. Removed the number and kept the qualitative point that coastal building continues.
findings.evidence: no source located in ONS, MHCLG or Environment Agency publications

findings.claim: At Mappleton in Holderness, a sea wall and rock groynes protected the village from 1991 onwards
findings.truth: The 1991 Mappleton scheme was two rock groynes plus a rock revetment at the cliff foot, at about GBP 2 million. There is no sea wall. Corrected in the text and in the model answer.
findings.evidence: standard Holderness case-study record of the 1991 scheme

findings.claim: Examiners reward cost-benefit thinking
findings.truth: Invented claim about examiner behaviour. Reworded to state what earns marks without speaking for examiners.
findings.evidence: house rule on fabricated examiner claims

findings.claim: if the average value of property protected is GBP 200,000 per home, the upgrade cost is roughly 1% of the property value protected over its lifetime
findings.truth: The worked example is wrong by an order of magnitude. 1,800 homes x GBP 200,000 = GBP 360 million; the GBP 38 million upgrade is 10.6% of that. Corrected to roughly 10%.
findings.evidence: recomputation from the figures given in the same paragraph

findings.claim: For the 8-mark Examine question on flood management, examiners reward balanced answers
findings.truth: Wrong command word and an invented examiner claim in one sentence. Both corrected.

findings.truth: Wrong command word. Changed to Assess.

findings.claim: Cleveland coalfields by the 1990s
findings.truth: Cleveland was an ironstone district, not a coalfield. The coalfield of the North East is the Durham coalfield, whose last pit, Wearmouth, closed in 1993. Corrected.
findings.evidence: Durham coalfield closure record; Cleveland ironstone district

findings.claim: Today around 14% of the UK population is foreign-born
findings.truth: The 2021 and 2022 UK censuses count 10.7 million residents born abroad, about 16% of the UK population. Corrected to 16%.
findings.evidence: ONS / census 2021-22 foreign-born population

findings.claim: Net international migration to the UK has averaged around 250,000 a year for two decades.
findings.truth: True for the 2010s but not for the last two decades. ONS records a record 944,000 in the year to March 2023, and 204,000 in the year to June 2025. Rewritten to give the 2010s level and the peak.
findings.evidence: ONS long-term international migration estimates

findings.claim: as Honda did in 2019, closing the Swindon plant
findings.truth: Honda announced the closure in February 2019; the plant built cars until July 2021. Corrected in the text, the flashcard answer and the model answer.
findings.evidence: Honda UK closure announcement 2019, production ended 2021

findings.claim: examiners reward chains of reasoning
findings.truth: Invented claim about examiner behaviour. Reworded.
findings.evidence: house rule on fabricated examiner claims

findings.claim: Birmingham's population grew from 1,003,000 in 2001 to 1,144,000 in 2021. ... = 14.06%
findings.truth: The 2001 census counted 977,091 people in Birmingham; the city did not pass one million again until after 2001. With the census figures the increase is 167,000 and the answer is 17.1%, not 14.1%. Question and answer key both corrected.
findings.evidence: census counts: 1991 1,005,764; 2001 977,091; 2011 1,073,045; 2021 1,144,900 (Wikipedia demography table, ONS census); recomputation

findings.claim: For the 8-mark Examine question on a UK city, examiners reward depth on a single named example

findings.claim: London's Docklands ... employing over 150,000 people
findings.truth: Canary Wharf itself reports about 120,000 workers. The wider Docklands total may reach 150,000 but no source confirms it. The figure repeats in the exam tip, a model answer and a flashcard, so it is recorded rather than edited piecemeal.
findings.evidence: Canary Wharf Group published employment figure

findings.claim: Online retail rose from around 5% of UK retail spending in 2008 to over 28% by 2023.
findings.truth: The ONS internet sales ratio averaged about 26% across 2023, peaking above 30% only in some months. 'Over 28%' is slightly high but within rounding of the monthly range.
findings.evidence: ONS internet sales as a percentage of total retail sales

findings.claim: FDI has averaged GBP 100bn/year, making the UK one of the world's largest investment destinations.
findings.truth: Annual inward FDI flows swing widely and typically sit well below GBP 100 billion; the stock, not the flow, is the large number. The lesson text hedges this as 'in good years', which is defensible, so only the model-answer bullet overstates it.
findings.evidence: ONS foreign direct investment statistics

findings.claim: The National Farmers' Union estimates that around half of UK farm businesses now earn money from non-farming activities.
findings.truth: Defra's Farm Business Survey puts diversification in England nearer two-thirds of farm businesses, and the attribution to the NFU is unverified. 'Around half' understates rather than overstates, so no edit.
findings.evidence: Defra Farm Business Survey diversification statistics

summary: Ten lessons checked against the spec. One systematic exam error runs through the unit: eight-mark questions and exam tips use the command word 'Examine', which is not one of this board's twelve command words, and six exam tips invent examiner behaviour. Two hard errors: the Foss Barrier cost-benefit worked example is out by a factor of ten, and the Birmingham population calculation starts from a 2001 figure the census does not support, so its answer key is wrong. Smaller factual fixes cover flood-risk properties versus people, the Mappleton scheme, the Durham coalfield, foreign-born share, net migration and the Honda Swindon dates.
